facts.text: High Court of Madras dismissed applications filed by the appellants for quashing charges under ss. 500 and 501 of the Penal Code framed by the Presidency Magistrate, Madras.

anchor.surface_text: These appeals, founded on special leave, are directed against the judgment of the learned Single Judge of the High Court of Madras dismissing the applications filed by the appellants for quashing charges under ss. 500 and 501 of the Penal Code framed by the Presidency Magistrate, Madras.

facts.text: Dravida Kazhagam has a membership of about 4000 persons in Madras city and elsewhere.

anchor.surface_text: The Dravida Kazhagam, a party having a platform for social reforms, has, according to counsel for the respondent, a membership of about 4000 persons in Madras city and elsewhere.

facts.text: Dravida Kazhagam sponsored and organised a conference held on January 23 and 24, 1971.

anchor.surface_text: The party sponsored and organised a conference, which held its sessions on January 23 and 24, 1971. The conference passed a number of resolutions,

facts.text: Conference passed resolution: It should not be made an offence for a person's wife to desire another man.

anchor.surface_text: the one relevant for these appeals was, as translated in English, by the High Court, as follows It should not be made an offence for a persons wife to desire another man.

facts.text: Appellants are editors and publishers of Dinamani, Hindu and Indian Express, printed and published in Madras.

anchor.surface_text: The appellants are and were at the material time the editors, and publishers of three daily newspapers, the Dinmani, the Hindu and the Indian Express, all printed and published in Madras.

facts.text: News item published in Hindu and other papers on January 25 and 26, 1971: Conference passed resolution requesting Government to make meeting another man's wife an offence.

anchor.surface_text: In the issues of January 25 and 26, 1971 there appeared in the Hindu, as also in the other two papers, a news item under the caption Demonstration against the Obscene Tableau in which among other things was published the following .lm15 The Conference passed a resolution requesting the Government to take suitable steps to see that meeting another mans wife is made an offence under the Indian Penal Code.

facts.text: News item reported demonstration by 300 persons against procession with obscene tableau depicting Hindu deities.

anchor.surface_text: The news item reported that about 300 persons had staged a black flag demonstration against the procession taken out in connection with the said conference in which tableau alleged to be obscene and depicting certain Hindu deities and mythological figures formed part.

facts.text: E. V. Ramaswami Naicker presided over the conference inaugurated by C.D. Naidu.

anchor.surface_text: The news item further reported that E. V. Ramaswami Naicker, the leader of the Dravida Kazhagam, seated in a tractor, was at the rear of the procession. He also presided over the said conference which was inaugurated by one C.D. Naidu.

facts.text: Respondent sent letter on January 28, 1971 to editor of Hindu demanding correction.

anchor.surface_text: On January 28, 1971, the respondent, signing as the chairman of the reception committee of the said conference, called upon the editor of the Hindu to publish a correction and clarification

facts.text: Hindu published clarification on February 1971 under caption Salem Conference Resolutions.

anchor.surface_text: On February 1971, the Hindu published the said clarification as demanded by the respondent under the caption Salem Conference Resolutions together with the version of its own representative at Salem

facts.text: Respondent's advocates letter on February 1, 1971 demanding apology.

anchor.surface_text: On February 1, 1971, the respondent, by his Advocates letter, called upon the editor to publish the correct text of the resolution stating that what was published in the Hindu was not only a travesty of truth but also highly defamatory

facts.text: Respondent filed complaints on February 9, 1971 against editors and publishers under ss. 500 and 501 IPC.

anchor.surface_text: No such apology having been tendered, the respondent filed complaints on February 9, 1971 against the editors and publishes of the three dailies under ss. 500 and 501 of the Penal Code in the Court of the Chief Presidency Magistrate, Madras.

facts.text: Respondent described himself as chairman of reception committee of the conference.

anchor.surface_text: In these complaints, the respondent described himself as an important member of the Dravida Kazhagam and of the Self-respect Movement organised by that party, as also an ardent disciple of its leader, the said E. V. Ramaswami Naicker. He further stated that the Dravida Kazhagam had organised the said conference

facts.text: Magistrate decided to issue process and proceed with trial.

anchor.surface_text: The Magistrate, on the basis of the complaint and the evidence he recorded, decided to issue process and to proceed with the trial.

facts.text: Appellants approached High Court under s. 561A CrPC to quash proceedings.

anchor.surface_text: The appellants in all, these appeals thereupon approached the High. Court under s. 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the said proceedings.

facts.text: Supreme Court allowed appeals, set aside High Court order, quashed proceedings as complaint not competent.

anchor.surface_text: In these circumstances and for the reasons set out above, we allow these appeals, set side the order of the High Court and quash the proceedings taken out by the Magistrate on the ground that the respondents complaint was not competent.

facts.text: Conference organized on December 13, 1970 meeting where respondent selected as chairman of reception committee.

anchor.surface_text: In regard to the conference and its set up, he said that on December 13, 1970 a meeting was held for organising the conference. At that meeting one or two persons suggested that he should be the chairman of the reception committee,

facts.text: Conference consisted of comrades of the movement, sympathisers, about 5000 women.

anchor.surface_text: He also deposed that the conference consisted of comrades of our movement, other social reform minded sympathisers and about 5000  women.

facts.text: Resolution moved by President Pariyar, no opposition, passed unanimously.

anchor.surface_text: Regarding the resolution in- question, he said that after the President Pariyar proposed nobody announced opposition to the resolution. The meaning is, that all approved.

facts.text: Court found conference separate body from Dravida Kazhagam with own organization, office, secretaries.

anchor.surface_text: Two facts clearly emerge from this evidence,  1  that though the conference was organised by the Dravida Kazhagam, it was a separate body with its own Organisation and office where correspondence relating to it was received and dealt with and had its own secretaries,

facts.text: News item did not mention respondent or sponsors by name.

anchor.surface_text: A persual of the news items shows that it concerned. itself with the protest demonstration against the procession taken, out on that occasion and the tableau,presented in the procession, the resolution in question passed at the conference held there,after and the fact of the said E. V. Ramaswami Naicker having presided over that conference.

facts.text: Respondent claimed he scrutinised and shaped draft resolution sent by Pariaswami.

anchor.surface_text: In the evidence he gave before the Magistrate on May 22, 1971, the respondent claimed that it was he, who, as the chairman of the reception committee of the conference, had scrutinised and given shape to the draft resolution sent at the conference for being-moved thereat,

facts.text: High Court held Dravida Kazhagam identifiable group, respondent aggrieved person.

anchor.surface_text: The Dravida Kazhagam is an identifiable group, The complainant is a member of this Kazhagam. He was the Chairman of the Reception Committee in the conference. He is active member of the Dravida Kazhagam.
